Internal: the note for a text variable's missing cells that a format writes as blank text

Source: R/io.R
dot-jst_jsave_text_na_note.Rd

Ruling R13 (Jeff, S345; built Session 351). SPSS format (.sav), Stata format (.dta), SAS interchange format (.xpt) and CSV format (.csv) have no missing value for text: haven and write.csv() write a text variable's NA as an empty string, and jload() reads that back as the <blank> category, counted as valid (the S340 decision: a blank is reported, never assumed missing, and a file cannot say which blanks were once missing). So jsave() says so when it happens: the variables, the cells, and the two formats that keep them (.rds, .xlsx). The .xpt format and a factor in a CSV file (written as its labels) lose the same way, probed at S351 and added on Jeff's lean. A missing NUMBER survives every format. A loss note, as the label and declaration losses are: not gated to the joutput() levels.

Usage

.jst_jsave_text_na_note(data, ext)

Arguments

data

The data frame as written.

ext

Lowercase target extension.

Value

The note, or NULL when the format keeps text NA or the frame has none.
